Context
-------
Read .github/copilot-instructions.md first.

Everything in the demo is now built. The presenter needs two documents,
both generated from the actual repository state so they cannot drift
from reality:

  docs/demo-runbook.md          the beat-by-beat script
  slides/speaker-notes.md       the Slidev speaker notes, one section
                                per slide

These documents are generated LOCALLY, from the repo. Do not invent
commands, metric names, panel titles, or script behaviour. Read the
actual files and reflect what is there.

Generation rules
----------------
1. Every command in the runbook must be verified against the script it
   calls. If the runbook says `./break.sh latency`, then break.sh must
   have a latency case. If not, do not write it — instead add a line to
   docs/runbook-gaps.md naming the mismatch.

2. Every metric name in the runbook must be checked against:
   - manifests/alert-rules.yaml
   - dashboards/*.yaml
   - the /metrics output of the running app, if reachable
   If a name in a dashboard does not appear anywhere else, flag it in
   docs/runbook-gaps.md as "unverified name".

3. Every panel name in the runbook must match a panel in the Perses
   dashboards.

4. Every "point at the screen" instruction must name which tab and
   which panel by title.

5. Speaker notes are prose, in the presenter's voice, written to be
   read aloud. Not fragments. Not bullets. Complete sentences.

6. Do not add personality, humour, or motivational filler. This
   audience is technical and will notice.

docs/demo-runbook.md structure
------------------------------
For each of the nine beats:

  ## Beat N — <name> · <start>–<end>
  **Screen:** <tab and panel, by title>
  **Do:**
    <the exact commands, copied from the actual scripts or manifests>
  **Say:**
    <the narration, in prose, using the metric names as they actually
     exist in this repo>
  **Point at:**
    <specific panels, by title>
  **Contingency:**
    <what to do if this beat fails. Every beat has one. If you
     cannot find a sensible contingency, write "no live contingency —
     on failure, advance to the next beat and narrate">.
  **Cut table entry:**
    <duration; whether it can be cut and in what order>

Then, at the end:
  ## Cut lines
    A table: beat, nominal duration, cut priority. State explicitly
    that beat 4 (DNS/policy) is never cut.
  ## Pre-demo checklist
    Everything that must be true before doors. Verified against
    preflight.sh's actual assertions.
  ## Post-demo reset
    The exact commands to return to a clean state, sourced from
    reset.sh and break.sh baseline.

slides/speaker-notes.md structure
---------------------------------
One section per slide, in slide order, using the actual slide titles
from slides/slides.md:

  ## Slide N — <title>
  <spoken prose, one paragraph per idea, in presenter's voice>

For the three demo interstitial slides, replace the prose with a single
directive sentence: "Advance to Beat N — see docs/demo-runbook.md."

Also write slides/notes-import.md, containing the exact HTML comment
blocks to paste into slides/slides.md if the presenter wants the notes
inline rather than as a separate file. Preserve the existing frontmatter
comments — do not duplicate notes that are already there.

docs/runbook-gaps.md
--------------------
A short, honest list of everything the runbook could not verify:
  - commands referenced but not present in scripts
  - metric names that appear in only one place
  - panels referenced but not found in dashboards
  - any assertion in the prompt above that could not be satisfied

If the list is empty, the file says "no gaps found" and nothing else.
Do not pad it. Do not invent gaps. An empty list is a good outcome.

Constraints
-----------
- Do not modify any script, manifest, dashboard, or chart.
- If a mismatch is found, write it to docs/runbook-gaps.md. Do not
  silently fix it. The presenter will decide.
- Do not modify slides/slides.md. Only produce the external notes file
  and the import-paste file.
- Both documents must be usable offline. All commands must work with
  the network interface down.

Acceptance
----------
1. docs/demo-runbook.md exists and covers all nine beats, with the
   structure above.
2. slides/speaker-notes.md exists with one section per slide in
   slides/slides.md, in the same order.
3. docs/runbook-gaps.md exists. Its contents are accurate.
4. For every command in the runbook, the same command exists in the
   script it names. Verify by grepping.
5. Report any gaps found. If none, say so explicitly.
